articles.title: 2027: Senator mobilises Cross River community for Tinubu
articles.summary: Eteng who currently represents Cross River Central Senatorial District under the All Progressives Congress (APC), received a rousing reception as hundreds of residents escorted him through major streets of the community.
articles.hausa_translation: 2027: Senatà ya kaita jama'a Cross River don Tinubu. Eteng wanda ya kasance wakili Cross River Central Senatorial District a gida APC ya karbi karbaši mai daɗi yayin da ɗarizon jama'a suka ramshi shi a cikin manyan tituna na gida.
critical_questions: Who funded and organized this mobilization event, and what are the financial flows involved?
Why is a 2027 campaign being launched in 2024/2025 when elections are three years away—what strategic advantage does early mobilization serve?
Whose voices are missing: did independent observers verify the 'hundreds' claim, and what do opposition parties or rival candidates say about this event?
Does Senator Eteng have stated ambitions to run in 2027, or is this framing imposed by the headline to boost Tinubu's image?
What is the ownership structure of PM News, and does it have documented APC political affiliations that might bias coverage?

articles.title: Nigerian troops kill 71 terrorists in nationwide offensive
articles.summary: The operations include a five-hour counter-offensive at Buni Yadi, Yobe, which reportedly accounted for 48 ISWAP fighters, as well as separate air and maritime strikes that neutralised 23 terrorists.
articles.hausa_translation: Sojojin Najeriya sun kashe 'yan ta'adda 71 a cikin bugi na kididdigida
critical_questions: What independent verification exists for the casualty figures, and who conducted the count?
Why are specific locations like Buni Yadi named for some operations but not others, and what accounts for the discrepancy in reported fighter numbers?
Whose voices are missing from this narrative - have affected civilians or independent observers been consulted about the operations?
What is the track record of previous casualty claims by Nigerian military, and have past figures been independently verified?
How do these operations fit into the broader security strategy, and what metrics indicate progress toward reducing terrorist activity?

articles.title: Why we deployed ‌‌‌electric instead of CNG buses in Abia – Otti
articles.summary: Otti said that CNG was cheaper to use than petrol and expressed optimism that the conversion of petrol and diesel vehicles to CNG would gain more traction in the country.
articles.hausa_translation: Me ya bayyana dalilin da ya sa mun bugi motocin lantarki maimakon motocin CNG a Abia – Otti. Otti ya ce CNG ya fi whanne fiye ga man petrol kuma ya nuna jiya cewa juyawa da motocin petrol da diesel zuwa CNG za su sami karfi a kasar.
critical_questions: Who funded the electric bus procurement and what are the financial terms versus the CNG alternative costs analysis?
Why does the headline emphasize electric deployment while the summary contradicts it by promoting CNG as cheaper?
What independent verification exists for claims that CNG conversion will 'gain traction' when infrastructure and adoption remain limited?
Are there commercial interests or partnerships with electric vehicle suppliers influencing this policy decision?
Where are the voices of transport operators, commuters, and energy experts in evaluating these competing technologies?

articles.title: FOLA: Rise Of Afrobeats Next Superstar
articles.summary: Fast-rising artiste Folarin Odunlami, known professionally as Fola, is already showing the trappings of an Afrobeats superstar. He began releasing music around 2018 and 2019, steadily putting out songs that hinted at a rare instinct for melody and emotion. Early tracks such as Miss You, Money Chaser, and Feeling built a small but loyal audience […]
articles.hausa_translation: Fola: Tashin Sabon Superstar na Afrobeats - Matashin mumumunan Folarin Odunlami, wanda aka sani da Fola, yana nuna alamomi na babbar baje jiya a cikin Afrobeats. Ya fara sake jita wajen 2018 da 2019, yana ci gaba da fitar da waƙoƙi waɗanda suka nuna karfin haɓaka waƙa da motsin zuciya. Waƙoƙin farko kamar Miss You, Money Chaser, da Feeling sun gina karamé amma aminci jama'a.
critical_questions: Who owns Leadership publication and does it have connections to music industry stakeholders or promotional networks that could benefit from hyping emerging artists?
What metrics define 'fast-rising' and 'showing trappings of superstardom' - streaming numbers, chart positions, social media following - and are these figures provided or merely asserted?
Why feature this artist now specifically, and who initiated this coverage - the publication independently or through artist management/PR representation?
Are there competing narratives about other emerging Afrobeats artists that weren't selected for similar coverage, and what determines that editorial choice?
What evidence beyond three song titles and vague descriptions of 'loyal audience' supports the claim of superstar potential, versus promotional language?

articles.title: 7 Iconic Nigerian Street Dances That Transformed Afro-Pop Culture
articles.summary: In Nigerian music, a hit song rarely lands on its own; it usually arrives with a signature movement that takes over dance floors, street corners, and music videos. For more than two decades, local artistes have leveraged custom dance steps to launch records, turn street subcultures into national trends, and project Nigerian pop culture onto […]
articles.hausa_translation: Jita Damje Na Gida Na Nigeria 7 wanda Suka Canja Halin Afro-Pop Culture
critical_questions: Which specific artistes and record labels are profiting most from these dance trends, and how are royalties/credits distributed to originators?
Are these 'iconic' dances being appropriated by international artists without attribution or compensation to Nigerian creators?
What evidence supports the claim that dance steps are the primary driver of song success versus production quality, marketing budgets, or radio play?
Why does the article truncate mid-sentence without substantive analysis of the seven dances—is this incomplete reporting or clickbait framing?
Whose voices are missing: street dancers, choreographers, and grassroots communities who likely created these moves before artistes commercialized them?

Ogunsola, through her solicitors, Bayo Osipitan and Co, demanded the removal of the publication, a retractio
articles.hausa_translation: Badirin UNILAG ya baida barazanar ₦1 biliyar akan labarin da ya nuna cewa jami'an jami'ar suka karɓi ₦397 miliyar cikin bayar rashin daidai yake, yayin da ₦434 miliyar jarin kuɗi ba a maimaita ba. Badirin Profesa Folasade Tolulope Ogunsola ta aika gida jiya ta neman kawar da labarin, ƙarƙashewa da takaitawa.

What is NaijaOnPoint's sourcing and evidence base—are they reporting whistleblower claims, leaked documents, or public records, and what's their track record on such investigations?
Is the ₦1bn suit amount proportionate to reputational harm, and does it follow a pattern of Nigerian institutional leaders using defamation threats to silence financial scrutiny?

articles.title: Hollywood Stars With Nigerian Roots: 10 Actors and Actresses Making Waves

Here are 10 internationally recognised actors […]

Whose voices and experiences are centered in this narrative critique - are marginalized perspectives within the story being dismissed as inadequate?
What is the timing of this negative review relative to the author's other works or public profile - could this reflect broader industry gatekeeping or personal conflicts?
Does the review distinguish between the author's artistic intent and execution, or does loaded language like 'futile' collapse this distinction to dismiss the entire work?

In May 2024, Somalia's President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud asked the UN to end the mission ahead of the expiry of its mandate in October that year. He later revised the request, proposing a two-year transition period.

articles.hausa_translation: Jami'ar Duniya Ta Kawo Da Aiki Ta Politika A Somaliya Bayan Shekaru 30
critical_questions: Why did President Mohamud reverse his initial request for immediate mission termination, and what political pressures influenced the proposal for a two-year transition instead?

articles.title: ‘Debt worse than leprosy’ – Obasanjo tackles Tinubu

articles.hausa_translation: Bashi ya fi cututtuka - Obasanjo ya kai hari ga Tinubu. 'Kowa da ya ce bashi ba cututtuka ba, abin daidai-daidaita ne. Bashi ya fi cututtuka domin cututtuka ta lalata mutum daya kawai. Bashi ya lalata tsofaffi'

articles.title: Navy marines kill 34 terrorists, disrupt ISWAP/Boko Haram operations in Lake Chad
articles.summary:
Nigerian Navy Marines at the Naval Base Lake Chad in conjunction with 403 Amphibious Brigade Nigerian Army, operating under Operation Hadin Kai, have recorded significant operational gains against Boko Haram Terrorists (BHT) in the Lake Chad area, neutralising 34 ISWAP/Boko Haram terrorists in the waters.
The post Navy marines kill 34 terrorists, disrupt ISWAP/Boko Haram operations in Lake Chad ap
articles.hausa_translation: Jiyun Soji na Nigeria ya kashe 'yan ta'adda 34, tacewa ISWAP/Boko Haram a Lake Chad - Jami'an Jiyun Soji na Nigeria a Naval Base Lake Chad tare da 403 Amphibious Brigade na Soji na Kasa, aiki karkashin Operation Hadin Kai, sun samu nasarori masu mahimmanci a kasar Lake Chad, suka kashe 'yan ta'adda 34 na ISWAP/Boko Haram a ruwan Lake Chad.
critical_questions: What independent verification exists for the claim of 34 terrorists killed, and who conducted the verification?
Why does this report lack specific dates, locations, and named military commanders, and what does this omission suggest about transparency?
How do these claimed casualties compare to historical patterns of military claims in Operation Hadin Kai, and have previous claims been independently verified?
What is the source's relationship to the military, and does Vanguard have editorial independence from government security narratives?
What are the humanitarian implications and civilian impact in the Lake Chad operational area that this military-focused narrative excludes?

articles.title: Iran’s army warns any new US attack would spread war wider
